title: Exact Accumulated-Field Determined Steady States with Boundary-Controlled Relaxation in Dissipative Quantum Link Chains
authors: Yazhuang Miao, Weizh Ma, Yong Wang, Xiaolong Zhao, Xuexi Yi
abstract: In open quantum lattice systems, changing the boundary condition would appear to alter both the steady state and the nonzero Liouvillian spectrum. Here we show that these two boundary-induced changes do not necessarily occur together in a globally reciprocal dissipative quantum link chain. The steady state is determined by an accumulated field defined by link-resolved dissipative asymmetries, and a gauge-generated transformation built from this field gives exact symmetry-resolved steady states with nonuniform, accumulated-field-dependent reduced matter occupations. We then construct a reciprocal cyclic boundary condition that preserves these matter occupations while changing the nonzero Liouvillian spectrum. Consequently, open and cyclic chains relax to the same reduced matter steady-occupation profile with different Liouvillian gaps, with the cyclic closure accelerating relaxation. In the strong-dissipation limit, this relaxation difference can be reduced to a spectral comparison of effective exclusion processes with open and cyclic boundaries.
summary: The paper analyzes dissipative quantum link chains to decouple the steady-state properties from their relaxation dynamics. It shows that while boundary conditions can be modified (e.g., from open to cyclic) to maintain the same reduced matter occupation profile, they fundamentally change the system's Liouvillian spectrum and thus its approach rate to equilibrium. This separation is controlled by an accumulated field derived from local dissipation asymmetries.
main_problem: The study investigates whether changes in boundary conditions (open vs. cyclic) affect both the steady state and the non-zero Liouvillian spectrum independently in dissipative quantum link chains.
main_result: The accumulated field, derived from local dissipation asymmetries, determines the exact reduced matter steady state, while a reciprocal cyclic closure can preserve this steady occupation but significantly alter the relaxation rates (Liouvillian gap).
method: The authors use gauge-generated transformations to find symmetry-resolved steady states and compare Liouvillian spectra by analyzing the time evolution of deviations from equilibrium.
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional U(1) quantum link chain subjected to dissipation, modeled via a Lindbladian superoperator. The dynamics are analyzed in the fixed-matter number sector.
key_observables: Reduced matter steady occupation ($\langle n angle_{ss}$), Liouvillian spectrum eigenvalues ($\lambda$), and relaxation rates ($\kappa_\eta$).
important_parameters: Link-resolved dissipative asymmetries ($h_n$), the accumulated field ($X_n$), and the strong-dissipation limit.
main_assumptions: The analysis often projects onto a fixed eigenvalue $N$ of the total matter number operator $\hat{N}$.
figures_summary: Figures compare steady occupations ($\langle n angle_{ss}$) for OBC vs. CBC, showing agreement in occupation but divergence in Liouvillian spectra and relaxation rates; Fig 4 compares fitted decay rates to spectral gaps.
paper_structure: The paper establishes that the accumulated field dictates the steady state via a gauge transformation. It then constructs a cyclic boundary condition that preserves this steady state profile while modifying the non-zero Liouvillian spectrum, demonstrating a separation between steady-state control and relaxation dynamics.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical framework for separating the determination of equilibrium states from the rates at which those states are approached in open quantum systems, highly relevant for understanding engineered dissipation.
